section_summary: This section combines wartime and postwar records on suspected Japanese espionage, propaganda, collaboration, and intelligence collection. It includes an FBI investigation of Spanish bullfighter José Amorós Cervigón, public inquiries about alleged broadcasts by Japanese Christian Toyohiko Kagawa, investigations of a Spanish theatrical company in Argentina and Filipino laborers sent to Hawaii, and extensive Strategic Services Unit reports on Japanese military intelligence personnel and operations in Europe and China. The final pages begin a biographical study of Major General Makoto Onodera that continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notices for restricted item 894.20200/1-1545
subfiles.about: Records the withdrawal of a January 15, 1945 item because of access restrictions.
subfiles.summary: The notices identify file item 894.20200/1-1545 as having been removed during archival review. The stated basis is security-classified or otherwise restricted information, under an authority dated April 19, 1976; the second page is an otherwise blank duplicate form.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning José Amorós Cervigón
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Chief, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on José Amorós Cervigón and his alleged recruitment by Ángel Alcázar de Velasco for Japanese intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports Amoros admitted being approached in Madrid by Angel Alcazar de Velasco to work for Japanese intelligence but denied accepting; Alcazar allegedly ran agents in the Western Hemisphere.

subfiles.title: Interrogation report on José Amorós Cervigón
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation source reporting from Trinidad
subfiles.about: Reports the shipboard interrogation and search of Spanish bullfighter José Amorós Cervigón during his journey to Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Amoros interrogated in Trinidad: he describes bullfighting, wartime service and Alcazar's offer to work for Japanese intelligence, which he says he refused; searches found nothing; Alcazar described as an Axis spy recruiter.

subfiles.title: Visa Division request for name check on Tomás Rojas del Castillo
subfiles.about: Requests a departmental and intelligence-agency name check on Tomás Rojas del Castillo.
subfiles.summary: Visa Division asks State, CIA, FBI and others for any information on Tomas Rojas del Castillo, enclosing a Panama operations memorandum.

subfiles.title: Panama operations memorandum concerning transit visas
subfiles.about: Provides identifying and passport information for Spanish travelers associated with a transit-visa inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Panama memo lists two Spanish nationals (apparently Rojas del Castillo and Amoros Cervigon) with passports and transit status; a transit visa was authorized January 11, 1952.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Erick Kendall about Kagawa and Topping
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Erick Kendall, editor, The Cooperative Builder
subfiles.about: Answers questions about alleged propaganda broadcasts by Toyohiko Kagawa and Helen Topping.
subfiles.summary: Dickover says monitored Tokyo broadcasts attributed anti-American statements and Christian work to Kagawa, but the Department cannot verify he spoke; he distinguishes Helen Topping from Mrs. Henry Topping.

subfiles.title: Erick Kendall's inquiry concerning Toyohiko Kagawa and Helen Topping
subfiles.from: Erick Kendall, editor, The Cooperative Builder
subfiles.to: Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests reliable information on reports that Kagawa and Helen Topping were engaged in anti-American propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Kendall asks about Kagawa's prewar tours, debate over his sincerity, the Newsweek claim that he was a Japanese propagandist, and whether Helen Topping took part in anti-American work.

subfiles.title: Newsweek clipping, “Kagawa: From preacher to propagandist?”
subfiles.about: Defends Newsweek's report that Kagawa supported the Japanese war effort while acknowledging uncertainty about coercion.
subfiles.summary: Newsweek clipping 'Kagawa: From preacher to propagandist?' cites State and FCC files, Kagawa's work among Filipinos and an August 7, 1944 anti-American broadcast, conceding voluntariness is undeterminable.

subfiles.title: Milo S. Hinkle inquiry concerning Kagawa
subfiles.from: Milo S. Hinkle, Plainfield Friends Meeting
subfiles.about: Asks whether the identification of Toyohiko Kagawa as an anti-American broadcaster has been established beyond doubt.
subfiles.summary: Hinkle cites Newsweek's claims that Kagawa abandoned pacifism and asks whether another Japanese Kagawa made the broadcasts.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Milo S. Hinkle
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Milo S. Hinkle, Plainfield Friends Meeting
subfiles.about: States that the Department cannot verify broadcasts and activities attributed to Toyohiko Kagawa.
subfiles.summary: Dickover says monitored Tokyo reports tie Kagawa to Christian work in the Philippines and China and anti-American statements, but the Department cannot judge accuracy.

subfiles.title: Kate I. Hansen letter about Kagawa
subfiles.about: Requests authoritative information about what had happened to Toyohiko Kagawa during the war.
subfiles.summary: Hansen says audiences ask what became of Kagawa and asks Grew for information to clear uncertainty harming his reputation.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Kate I. Hansen
subfiles.about: Replies that reports and broadcasts attributed to Kagawa cannot be authenticated.
subfiles.summary: Dickover, at Grew's request, repeats that monitored Tokyo reports tie Kagawa to Christian work and criticism of the US, which the Department cannot evaluate.

subfiles.title: M. E. Dodd inquiry concerning Kagawa
subfiles.from: M. E. Dodd, General Director, Centennial Evangelistic Crusade
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests an assessment of reports that Kagawa broadcast propaganda and had acted as a Japanese spy in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Dodd, who hosted Kagawa in Shreveport, doubts the allegations but gets many inquiries, enclosing an editorial citing Newsweek and Dan Gilbert's espionage accusation.

subfiles.title: Clipping, “Being Jap”
subfiles.about: Reprints and endorses allegations that Toyohiko Kagawa was a Japanese spy masquerading as a Christian minister.
subfiles.summary: Editorial 'Being Jap' cites Newsweek's report of Kagawa's anti-American broadcasts and Gilbert's claim that he was a Japanese agent while lecturing in American churches.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to M. E. Dodd
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Responds to Dodd's questions about Kagawa's broadcasts and alleged prewar subversive activity.
subfiles.summary: Dickover repeats the Department cannot authenticate Tokyo radio statements attributed to Kagawa and has no information supporting claims of subversive activity in the US.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning Conchita Piquer's company
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on members of Conchita Piquer's theatrical company and a reported Japanese espionage approach.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends information on a Spanish theatrical company reportedly contacted by a Japanese espionage agent in Madrid before going to Buenos Aires.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Esteban Delgado Bernal and the Piquer company
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation sources in Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Reports surveillance of members of Conchita Piquer's company for possible Axis espionage connections.
subfiles.summary: FBI report on guitarist Esteban Delgado, manager Clemente and Marquez: no clear evidence of espionage, though two had contacts with suspected Axis agents; they hope to tour the US but had no visa applications.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Singapore concerning Andrew Kuo
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Singapore
subfiles.about: Transmits Andrew Kuo's account of Allied service and Japanese propaganda activities in Southeast Asia.
subfiles.summary: Department authorizes thanking Andrew Kuo for wartime activities, retaining his account of Japanese propaganda in Southeast Asia.

subfiles.title: Gantenbein memorandum favoring transmission to Hawaii
subfiles.about: Argues that national-defense considerations justify sending the Manila warning about suspected collaborators to Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Gantenbein concedes Lockhart's objections but agrees the consul general's letter should go to the Governor of Hawaii promptly.

subfiles.title: Wellington memorandum on forwarding the Manila warning
subfiles.about: Recommends sending the suspected-collaborator information to Hawaii and the FBI despite identification problems.
subfiles.summary: Wellington argues that even non-identifiable adverse information should be placed in the hands of Hawaiian authorities. The memorandum also suggests asking Consul General Steintorf to assemble and forward any additional information about the named people.

subfiles.title: Lockhart memorandum opposing action on the Hawaii warning
subfiles.about: Recommends filing without action a vague warning about Filipino laborers sent to Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart opposes sending the Hawaii warning: it names no offenses or witnesses, and common Philippine names matched only a master suspect file, risking innocent suspicion.

subfiles.title: Routing note authorizing mailing
subfiles.from: State Department Far Eastern Affairs office
subfiles.about: Requests review and, absent objection, mailing of an attached communication.
subfiles.summary: Routing note authorizing mailing of attached Manila warning material about laborers sent to Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Steintorf letter warning of possible Filipino collaborators
subfiles.from: Paul P. Steintorf, American Consul General, Manila
subfiles.to: Ingram M. Stainback, Governor of Hawaii
subfiles.about: Lists Filipino laborers aboard the SS Marine Falcon whose names matched records of possible pro-Japanese collaboration.
subfiles.summary: Steintorf warns twenty-two Vigan laborers sent to Hawaii may have collaborated with Japan, based only on matching a manifest against a confidential file; Hawaii should investigate.

subfiles.title: State Department transmittal of the Manila warning to Interior
subfiles.about: Forwards the consul general's confidential warning for transmission to the Governor of Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: State sends Interior Steintorf's July 29 warning on Filipino laborers, acknowledging meager information; Manila asked for a supplementary report.

subfiles.title: Instruction requesting a supplementary Manila report
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Manila
subfiles.about: Requests additional information about the laborers named in Steintorf's letter to the Governor of Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Instruction asks Manila to obtain supplementary information on the named individuals.

subfiles.title: Interior Department acknowledgment of transmission to Hawaii
subfiles.from: Edwin G. Arnold, Department of the Interior
subfiles.to: Frank P. Lockhart, Department of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that Steintorf's confidential letter was forwarded to Governor Stainback.
subfiles.summary: Interior tells Lockhart it sent the July 29 Manila letter to the Governor of Hawaii.

subfiles.title: State Department transmittal of supplementary collaboration report
subfiles.about: Forwards Manila's October 11 supplementary report for the information of Interior and the Governor of Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: State sends Interior and Hawaii the supplementary Manila report on Filipinos carried on the Marine Falcon.

subfiles.title: Manila supplementary report on alleged Filipino collaboration
subfiles.from: Paul P. Steintorf, American Consul General, Manila
subfiles.about: Explains the weak evidentiary basis for the earlier warning about Filipino laborers sent to Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Steintorf clarifies the master file was an Army CIC roster of pro-Japanese organizations, so a name was not proof; common names risked misidentification; the warning was only guidance.

subfiles.title: SSU transmittal of three intelligence reports
subfiles.from: Chief, Dissemination Branch, Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.to: Jack Neal, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.about: Forwards three classified SSU reports believed to be of interest to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: SSU sends Jack Neal reports DB-1246, DB-1233 and DB-1228 on Japanese intelligence personnel in Stockholm, attaché funds and a 1939 peace initiative.

subfiles.title: Biographical sketches of Japanese military-attaché assistants in Stockholm
subfiles.about: Profiles five assistants to Makoto Onodera and describes their wartime economic, technical, procurement, coding, and liaison work.
subfiles.summary: Based on Sugamo Prison interrogations, the report profiles Yoichi Inoue, Kiyokazu Ito, Yasukazu Kigoshi, Kichinosuke Sato, and Tatsuya Sato. It describes their education and assignments in Berlin, Rome, and Stockholm; collection from publications and business contacts; procurement of ball bearings, piano wire, and other war materials; coding; and liaison with German, Finnish, Polish, and other intelligence contacts. Although the report judges most of the men to have played subsidiary intelligence roles, it recommends further questioning of Kigoshi about the possible concealment of secret funds.

subfiles.title: Possible diversion of Japanese attaché funds to postwar intelligence recruits
subfiles.about: Examines Onodera's proposal to finance Hungarian and Finnish students as potential postwar Japanese intelligence recruits.
subfiles.summary: As Germany collapsed, Onodera asked Voeczkoendy to find young Hungarian scientists to move to Sweden on Japanese funds as a future intelligence service; similar Finnish plans were discussed but not implemented.

subfiles.title: Historical note on proposed 1939 Sino-Japanese negotiations
subfiles.about: Records Onodera's claim that senior Japanese officers sought a negotiated settlement with Chongqing in early 1939.
subfiles.summary: Onodera said a Wang Jingwei puppet regime would harm Japanese policy; his proposed talks with Chongqing, opened through Chen Li-fu, were exposed by Colonel Kagesa, causing a scandal.

subfiles.title: SSU transmittal of DB-1229 and DB-1226
subfiles.from: Chief, Dissemination Branch, Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.to: Jack Neal, Division of Foreign Activity Correlation
subfiles.about: Forwards two classified biographical intelligence reports for State Department retention.
subfiles.summary: SSU sends Jack Neal reports DB-1229 and DB-1226 on Japanese intelligence officers in Finland and Major General Makoto Onodera.

subfiles.title: Biographical sketches of Japanese intelligence officers in Finland
subfiles.about: Presents heavily degraded biographical records of two Japanese officers involved in intelligence and cryptanalysis work in Latvia and Finland.
subfiles.summary: The report is based on Sugamo Prison interrogations, but the subjects' names and numerous details are obscured by poor OCR. The first officer served in Manchurian and Russian intelligence, became military attaché in Riga and Helsinki, and cooperated with Finnish and Baltic services; the narrative also describes agent networks, counterespionage in Harbin, and contacts in the Soviet consulate. The second officer was an artilleryman and code specialist trained in Russian cryptanalysis who served as a student officer and assistant military attaché in Finland before returning to the Imperial General Staff.

subfiles.title: Biographical sketch of Major General Makoto Onodera
subfiles.about: Begins a detailed biographical account of Japanese intelligence officer Makoto Onodera.
subfiles.summary: Biography of Onodera from German-language Sugamo interrogations in 1946: family, education, infantry service and Army Infantry School research, leading to his 1931-33 Russian Section work; continues beyond page 67.
